parallel.requirements: Recognized the exact Python-to-Node migration requirements: ESM .mjs files, local modules only, exact argv parsing, exact Fraction arithmetic and output, executable-only probing, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent retained implementation ownership, delegated an argparse behavioral-spec child, and later launched a broad verifier workflow with six fuzz/review children over numeric, argparse, environment, and repr surfaces.
parallel.implementation: The parent produced a multi-module manual implementation using custom integer limbs, rational arithmetic, argparse emulation, stdout/traceback handling, argv decoding, and an entry file in /output/test20.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote the final implementation tree into /output and artifact validation captured the expected entry and libraries, but the parent never produced a final response because the process timed out.
parallel.verification: The parent probed samples and many error paths, used the argparse child spec, ran differential checks, launched broad workflow verification, and found at least one late edge diff before timeout; the workflow aggregate never returned.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official artifact passed 146/146, but the parallel process ended by timeout with an empty final response, an unfinished verifier workflow, one errored verifier child, and at least one self-observed edge divergence left unclosed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same task requirements, including exact command-line behavior, exact rational output, ESM .mjs delivery, no npm dependencies, and executable-only probing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in a single parent trajectory with no delegation, so the same actor owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final response.
serial.implementation: Implemented a smaller module tree using native arbitrary-precision integers, rational arithmetic, pyint parsing, argparse formatting, traceback handling, and an entry point at /output/test20.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Assembled the /output tree, ensured imports and the entry point were present, and returned a final response containing the hierarchy, code excerpts, and verification notes.
serial.verification: Ran targeted differential tests, randomized fuzz cases, terminal-width checks, syntax/import checks, and byte comparisons against the reference binary, then reported those results in the final answer.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished work is recorded; the final notes disclose a judgment call about native arbitrary-precision integer use, but the official evaluator passed 146/146.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt's ESM, exact argv, exact Fraction output, no dependency, no Python, and /output placement requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the identical prompt and recognized the same required command-line, Fraction, module, dependency, and output constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No official requirement coverage difference explains the outcome; both artifacts satisfied the current evaluator, though parallel spent more effort exploring extra edge behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into parent implementation, one argparse-spec child, and a six-child workflow for verifier/reviewer coverage after implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents or workflows; the parent alone owned implementation, testing, fixes, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced coordination and lifecycle surfaces around verifier work, while serial kept a single owner and avoided handoff or workflow-return dependencies.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried detailed task context, harness instructions, known deviations, and verifier scope; no incompatible cross-agent component contract was required because children were verifiers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context local in one trajectory and therefore had no cross-agent interface to transmit or reconcile.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's context boundary was large but explicit; the problem was lifecycle and budget exhaustion of the verifier workflow, not absent task context or incompatible component interfaces.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built many modules around a custom limb-based integer implementation, parser, fraction, runtime, traceback, argv, and source-map layers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a smaller module tree and final answer around native arbitrary-precision integers plus local argparse, rational, text, error, and wrapping modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths passed officially; parallel's implementation was broader and more custom, while serial's was more compact and easier to close within the run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The direct argparse child completed and was consumed, but the later workflow verifier lifecycle ended with null result and killed status while children were still in progress or errored.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and returned a complete final response after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost closure on a verifier workflow result; serial had a simple linear result lifecycle and no child-return dependency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the implementation tree and workflow children mostly read /output while using separate /tmp helpers; artifact validation found the expected final files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and delivered one coherent /output tree without concurrent workspace writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision or contamination explains task behavior; the important integration difference is that parallel's artifact was captured despite no final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local differential tests and launched broad workflow verification, but the workflow was killed before aggregate findings were verified or returned; official evaluation still passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed targeted differential, fuzz, terminal-width, syntax/import, and byte checks before returning its final message; official evaluation also passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more concurrent verification ambition but less closure; serial had narrower but completed verification and acceptance reporting.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used six workflow children plus one direct child, accumulated over four million tokens, hit the 2399-second timeout, and left final.txt empty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no children, finished in 1834.579 agent seconds with remaining budget, and returned a complete final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's broad concurrent verification consumed the closure budget; serial's single-threaded plan closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status.json evaluation records report solution_passed true and 146/146 passed samples. The concrete difference is that parallel passed via an artifact captured after a timed-out process and empty final response, while serial passed after a normal single-agent completion and final report.

Broad workflow verifier fan-out did not return before closure.
serial_contributors: Single parent kept implementation and verification local.

ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a custom limb-based integer implementation and had a late self-observed traceback-line edge divergence before timeout.

evaluator_effects: The official artifact evaluator accepted both captured output trees 146/146 even though the parallel agent process itself timed out.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern explains adverse parallel process closure only

candidates.reason: The parallel parent actively owned and wrote the implementation modules and entry point; implementation was not merely researched or left ownerless.

The deliverable entry file and libraries were assembled in /output and artifact validation found the expected test20.mjs entry.
The parent owned the build, local tests, workflow launch, and delivery pipeline; the adverse event was budget exhaustion after broad verification, not absent pipeline ownership.
Executable probing preceded implementation, but it was not a mandatory serial gate that blocked all productive work and left implementation unfinished.
The parent launched an argparse probe child and continued implementing; investigation was not completed as a separate phase before productive work began.
The indispensable implementation path had already produced a passing artifact; the adverse closure came from collective verifier fan-out, which is more specific.

The parallel parent launched a broad workflow with six verifier children and planned further review/verification phases; before it could return an aggregate result, one child hit an API-rate error, others were still in progress, and the parent process timed out.
candidates.realized_consequence: Verifier workflow results were not aggregated before timeout, leaving an empty final response and unfinished verifier children even though the captured artifact later passed official tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing verifier return is downstream of the same excessive workflow breadth and budget exhaustion, not a separate result-lifecycle episode.

No known finding or requirement is shown disappearing through summary or transfer; the completed direct child result was visible and used by the parent.
The verifier workflow never returned an aggregate handoff for the parent to reduce, so there was no oversized returned report that the parent failed to consume.
No receiver is shown acting on superseded workspace or requirement state; children tested the candidate state available in /output.
The parallel parent did not receive incompatible completed handoffs that it left unadjudicated; the broad workflow failed to aggregate before closure.
The parent did not present whole-task completion before closure; the final response was empty, and official evaluation happened after artifact capture rather than as a parent acceptance decision.
No replacement or retry child was launched without inherited findings or current workspace state, so there is no repeated-work retry episode.

Verifier return was absent, but the taxonomy instructs using Fan-out Budget Exhaustion when excessive workflow breadth consumes budget and the aggregate verifier result is the downstream terminal state.
The int-literals child error occurred inside the same broad verifier workflow that exhausted budget; no separate takeover episode with a distinct consequence is evidenced.
The completed direct argparse child result was consumed, and workflow partial findings were not returned as completed parent-visible results before closure.
The parent did not simply wait blindly; it continued independent verification while the workflow ran, and the timeout chain is better classified as broad verifier fan-out exhaustion.
No concurrent agents produced competing implementation files or overlapping designs that required reconciliation; workflow agents tested and reviewed the parent candidate.
No evidence shows two live agents editing the same source/configuration file or reconciling each other's same-file edit.
No agent replaced or wholesale rewrote non-entry source produced by another live implementation owner.
No child or concurrent actor overwrote the required test20.mjs deliverable while another agent owned or used it; the parent wrote the deliverable.
No cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree provenance.
Although several agents used /tmp helpers and read /output, no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from shared implementation workspace writes is proven.
The shared /tmp harness was an intentional verifier input, not accidental contamination; no agent consumed another temporary artifact as a false reference environment.
